O.content: No printed substantial-change threshold, routing cutoff, or follow-up decision rule is visible.
The endpoint markers aligned with 2005 and 2014 have inscriptions "23.9°C" and "10.1°C", respectively.

B.text: If substantial-change follow-up requires meeting an explicit threshold or other operational criterion, and no such criterion is displayed or supplied, the chart alone cannot establish that the full-period change requires substantial-change follow-up. If the workflow defaults unverified changes to routine monitoring, routine monitoring is appropriate.
B.conditions: Applies only if follow-up is threshold/criterion based and routine monitoring is the default when the criterion cannot be verified; neither condition is supplied.

O.location: leftmost plotted marker aligned with the 2005 x-axis tick
O.content: A black marker has the inscription "23.9°C" immediately above it.

O.location: rightmost plotted marker aligned with the 2014 x-axis tick
O.content: A black marker has the inscription "10.1°C" immediately above it.
The title reads "Regional Summer Temperature Trend" and the vertical-axis label reads "Temperature (°C)".

B.text: The chart title and axes indicate that each plotted marker represents regional summer temperature for its aligned year, and the °C inscriptions attached to markers provide the plotted values. If a full-period change is evaluated as the end-year value minus the start-year value, the printed endpoint values can be subtracted. If the routing program treats a temperature change of this magnitude as substantial without requiring a separately displayed threshold, it should enter substantial-change follow-up.
B.conditions: Applies to the 2005–2014 regional summer-temperature series; the final routing clause is an assumption because no substantial-change threshold or decision rule is supplied.
